determinism: Every frame is taken through setCaptureCameraPose with a FIXED visual clock (42000 ms) and seed (82031) and with bots cleared, so the sky, clouds, wind and lighting are identical pose-to-pose and run-to-run and the before/after sets are pixel-comparable.

rootCauseFound.headline: The mountains were not mis-coloured - their colour was being DELETED at runtime.
rootCauseFound.detail: legacy-main.ts::batchSelectedArenaPresentation runs batchPresentationRootOnce(neighbourhoodLifeRoot, "palette-lit") over the whole pass31-neighbourhood-life group long after nuketown-mountain-backdrop.ts has added itself to it. In palette-lit mode art-kit.ts::batchStaticMeshes keys the batch on the source material colour - 0xffffff for a vertexColors material - builds a fresh flat MeshLambertMaterial at that colour, and deletes every geometry attribute outside {position, normal}, the vertex COLOUR attribute with it. The shipped massif was therefore one merged, flat, PURE WHITE Lambert batch drawn from pass31-neighbourhood-life-render-batches, while nuketown-mountain-ridge / -foothills / -far-range sat at visible=false. Every altitude band, every tonal break-up and the snow lerp were all irrelevant: the shader never saw them. The fix is one line - group.userData.dynamic = true, the documented batchStaticMeshes opt-out that rain-presentation and the pass31 flower beds already use.
rootCauseFound.howItWasFound: A scene-graph probe found the three ridge meshes at visible=false while pale mountains were plainly on screen, and a mesh with world radius 133 m at y 15 sitting under pass31-neighbourhood-life-render-batches. Detaching the backdrop group changed nothing, because the backdrop group was not what was being drawn.
rootCauseFound.secondCause: Runtime fog was also inverting the ridge. The arena fog is 0xb1c0be (relative luminance 0.73) while the sunset sky measures 85-155/255 behind the massif, and at 96-132 m the linear fog factor is 0.58-0.82 - a floor above the sky that no albedo could get under. Measured both ways at the same poses: fog on gives ridge/sky 0.74 and 0.67, fog off with the haze baked per vertex gives 0.49 and 0.42.

ridgeSkyMethod:
Two masks, both derived from the after build at a FIXED camera pose, fixed visual time (42000 ms) and fixed seed (82031), so before and after frames are pixel-comparable.
  covered   = pixels that change when the nuketown-mountain-backdrop group is DETACHED from the scene. Detaching is the only removal that survives a frame here; setting .visible=false is overwritten by a per-frame presentation pass.
  ridgeSurface = covered AND repainted between before and after, i.e. the subset where the ridge is the VISIBLE surface rather than sitting behind the forest ring. This is the honest ridge-against-sky measurement; the wider "covered" set is diluted by the identical forest pixels in front of the massif and understates the before ratio.
sky = the same pixels in the backdrop-detached frame. ratio = ridge / sky.
The ridge GEOMETRY is unchanged between the two builds (same seed, same radii, same heights); only vertex colours, the material and the ground skirt moved, so one mask is valid for both.

frameCostOfWhatThisPassADDED.method: meanMs per 280-frame sample, 6 interleaved pairs per pose; interleaved A/B/A/B because the same session drifts 4.6 ms on its own.
frameCostOfWhatThisPassADDED.verdict: Under 0.25 ms at the worst pose (standing at a new yard tree with all eight trees, 53 understory clumps and 509 forest contact skirts in frame) and indistinguishable from zero down the lane. Well inside the 1 ms the brief asked to be justified.

framePacing.caveat: Chrome launched with --disable-gpu-vsync; without it every sample reads 16.7 ms and the question cannot be answered. Cross-run pacing drifts by several ms on this machine, so the interleaved A/B above is the load-bearing number, not this pair.

gameplaySafety.rationale: Nothing added inside the boundary reaches the 0.5 m that quality-composition-parity calls substantial, and nothing reaches a crouched player's ~1.1 m eye height: the new planting cannot read as cover and cannot hide a collider. The eight yard boles sit strictly inside the authored [0.68*scale, 4*scale, 0.68*scale] trunk colliders; branches and canopy start above a standing player. No colliders, shot surfaces or raycast meshes were added anywhere.
